claimed_root_cause: Leftover R2 management handlers gate on get_current_user only, while the documented and sibling owner control (_require_owner / can_manage_integrations / POST cors is_owner check) is omitted, so a catalogger JWT exercises the shared-bucket credential for ping write, CORS read, and own-account migrate.
title: Catalogger JWT can invoke leftover owner-documented R2 migrate, ping, and CORS-read ops
description: UI-less R2 management routes are authenticated but not owner-authorized. DEPLOY.md says POST /integrations/r2/migrate-catalog is account-owner ops. Sibling POST /integrations/r2/cors and can_manage_integrations require owner (cors also allows master-admin email). migrate_catalog_to_r2, r2_ping, and r2_cors_get stop at get_current_user. Clients are 403 via the HTTP allowlist. A same-account catalogger JWT can therefore (1) write and delete the shared-bucket key _health/r2-ping.txt through the API Account token, outside catalog/{account_id}/, (2) read the bucket-wide CORS rules and AllowedOrigins, and (3) start a local-to-R2 migrate of that account. Cross-tenant migrate still requires master-admin email. No handler was executed in this run.

trace.description: r2_ping depends on get_current_user only and then calls object_storage.ping when R2 vars are set.
JWT is bound to User via sub plus account_id; enforce_client_http runs, then the User is returned with no owner or can_manage_integrations check.
No /integrations/r2 path is allowlisted, so clients are 403; catalogger and owner are not clients and continue.
ping put_bytes then delete_object on _health/r2-ping.txt using the API R2 identity; that key is not under catalog/{account_id}/.

validation_plan.local: In an isolated dummy two-role fixture with R2 mocked (put_bytes/delete_object/get_bucket_cors/migrate_local_photos_to_r2), mint catalogger, owner, and client JWTs. GET /integrations/r2/ping, GET /integrations/r2/cors, and POST /integrations/r2/migrate-catalog as each role. Confirm client is 403; record whether catalogger is 200 while POST /integrations/r2/cors is 403. Assert the mocked ping key is _health/r2-ping.txt. Do not use live R2 credentials.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner-observed only: confirm leftover /integrations/r2/migrate-catalog, /ping, and GET /cors are still mounted and whether any catalogger is expected to call them. Do not invoke ping against the production bucket (it writes a shared key).

blockers: This run has no OS-enforced sandbox and forbids executing target code, so catalogger versus owner versus client status codes were not observed.
Whether a live tenant has catalogger users and R2 configured is an environment fact; this run must not call the public API or write the shared bucket.
No parent scratch-promotion procedure is available, so a local dummy-JWT check could not be recorded as an artifact.

evidence.description: Migrate is documented as POST /integrations/r2/migrate-catalog with auth as account owner and as an ops endpoint not shown in the Account UI.
migrate_catalog_to_r2 also Depends(get_current_user) only; is_owner is not called before migrate_local_photos_to_r2.
r2_cors_get is get_current_user only and returns CatalogR2CorsOut origins plus the raw bucket CORSRules.
Sibling POST /integrations/r2/cors requires is_owner(current) or is_master_admin_email before put_bucket_cors.
can_manage_integrations is owner-only; leftover R2 GET/migrate handlers do not call it.
_require_owner exists and is used on other account-admin routes but is not invoked by migrate, ping, or GET cors.
CatalogR2MigrateIn.account_id is commented as master admin only; owners always migrate their own account — the schema comment does not mention cataloggers, and the handler does not reject them.
The ping probe key is the literal _health/r2-ping.txt on the shared bucket.
